concepts.name: Definition and Legal Status of 'Climate Refugee' vs. '1951 Refugee Convention Refugee'
key_dimensions: 1951 Refugee Convention definition: persecution-based, excludes environmental displacement
Why climate refugees do NOT qualify under existing international refugee law — the critical legal gap
Distinction between 'refugee', 'asylum seeker', 'IDP (Internally Displaced Person)', and 'climate migrant'
UNHCR's position and reluctance to formally recognize 'climate refugee' as a legal category

concepts.name: 1951 Refugee Convention and 1967 Protocol: Applicability and Gaps for Climate Displacement
key_dimensions: Five grounds for refugee status (race, religion, nationality, political opinion, social group) — climate NOT included
Non-refoulement principle and its limited applicability to climate cases
Debate on expanding the Convention vs. creating a new legal instrument
UNHCR Advisory Opinion 2020 on climate change and statelessness as a partial workaround

concepts.name: Slow-Onset vs. Sudden-Onset Climate Events and Displacement Patterns
key_dimensions: Slow-onset: sea-level rise, desertification, glacial retreat, salinization — leads to gradual migration
Sudden-onset: cyclones, floods, storm surges — leads to emergency displacement
Why slow-onset displacement is harder to legally capture and politically address
IPCC classification and thresholds for each type; governance implications

concepts.name: Statelessness Due to Submersion: The Small Island Developing States (SIDS) Crisis
key_dimensions: Nations at existential risk: Tuvalu, Kiribati, Maldives, Marshall Islands — legal personality of a submerged state
UNCLOS and maritime zone rights if land territory disappears
Tuvalu–Australia 'Falepili Union' (2023): world's first climate migration treaty — key provisions
1954 Statelessness Convention and 1961 Convention on Reduction of Statelessness — applicability

concepts.name: Nansen Initiative and the 'Agenda for the Protection of Cross-Border Displaced Persons in the Context of Disasters and Climate Change'
key_dimensions: Origin: 2012 initiative by Switzerland and Norway; culminated in 2015 Protection Agenda
Platform on Disaster Displacement (PDD) as its successor mechanism
Non-binding nature and voluntary state commitments — key limitation
Nansen Passport (historical) vs. modern Nansen Initiative — UPSC confusion trap

concepts.name: Global Compact on Refugees (GCR) 2018 and Climate Change Nexus
key_dimensions: GCR's acknowledgment of climate, environmental degradation as displacement drivers — first UN soft-law recognition
Non-binding nature; adopted by UNGA (not a treaty)
Distinction from Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) 2018 — UPSC trap on which covers climate migrants
GCM Objective 2 explicitly addresses climate and environmental migration

concepts.name: Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) 2018: Climate Migration Provisions
key_dimensions: Objective 2: addresses climate, environmental and disaster-driven migration specifically
Concept of 'planned relocation' and 'migration as adaptation strategy'
Non-binding Marrakech Compact; US, Hungary non-signatories — geopolitical dimension
Distinction from GCR: GCM covers all migrants including climate; GCR only refugees — critical UPSC overlap

concepts.name: UNHCR's Operational Guidance and the 'Climate-Conflict Nexus'
key_dimensions: How climate stress amplifies conflict leading to refugee flows — indirect pathway to refugee status
Syria drought (2006–2010) as a case study linking climate stress to conflict-driven displacement
UNHCR's 2022 report: over 21.5 million people displaced annually by weather events
Legal argument: climate-conflict nexus as a potential pathway to qualify under 1951 Convention

concepts.name: Internal Displacement and the Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement (1998)
key_dimensions: Brookings–Bern Process; Guiding Principles are soft law, not legally binding
Definition of IDP vs. cross-border refugee — most climate displaced are IDPs, not refugees
IDMC (Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre) data: climate events displace more people internally than conflict
Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) overlap with IDP protection

concepts.name: Loss and Damage Mechanism and Climate Refugees: The COP28 Fund
key_dimensions: Loss and Damage Fund operationalized at COP28 (Dubai, 2023) — first dedicated fund
Connection between L&D and displacement: slow-onset losses as non-economic damages
Santiago Network for L&D (technical assistance) vs. the new L&D Fund — UPSC confusion trap
Financing gap: pledges vs. actual need for displacement-related losses

concepts.name: Planned Relocation as a Climate Adaptation Strategy: Ethics and Governance
key_dimensions: Definition: government-managed, permanent movement of communities — distinct from forced displacement
Case studies: Fiji's Vunidogoloa village relocation; Bangladesh coastal relocations; Kiribati land purchase in Fiji
IASC (Inter-Agency Standing Committee) Framework on Durable Solutions
Ethical tensions: consent, cultural identity loss, 'climate gentrification', livelihood disruption

concepts.name: Climate Justice and Responsibility: Polluter-Pays Principle Applied to Refugee Burden
key_dimensions: Historical emissions by developed nations vs. displacement burden borne by developing/vulnerable nations
CBDR-RC (Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities) principle — Paris Agreement linkage
Legal obligation argument: ICJ Advisory Opinion request by Vanuatu (2023) on state obligations re: climate change
Equity dimension: Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sub-Saharan Africa — high vulnerability, low emissions

concepts.name: ICJ Advisory Opinion on Climate Change (Requested by Vanuatu, 2023)
key_dimensions: UNGA Resolution A/77/276 requesting ICJ opinion on state obligations and consequences for displacement
Distinction between advisory opinion (non-binding) and contentious jurisdiction (binding)
Potential to clarify if climate displacement triggers non-refoulement or other obligations
ITLOS Advisory Opinion (May 2024): greenhouse gases as marine pollution — related legal development

concepts.name: Ioane Teitiota Case (2020): UN Human Rights Committee Landmark Decision
key_dimensions: First international ruling linking climate change to human rights in context of deportation
New Zealand's deportation of Kiribati national — committee ruled against Teitiota but established future threshold
ICCPR Article 6 (right to life) as a potential protection basis for climate migrants
Key nuance: committee said threshold of 'real risk of irreversible harm' must be imminent — UPSC trap

concepts.name: Regional Frameworks and Agreements Addressing Climate Displacement
key_dimensions: Kampala Convention (African Union, 2009): first legally binding treaty protecting IDPs including from natural disasters
Cartagena Declaration (1984): broader refugee definition covering 'massive violations of human rights' — Latin America
Pacific Framework: Pacific Resilience Meeting (PRM) and Pacific Islands Forum climate mobility discussions
EU Temporary Protection Directive: designed for mass influx — debated applicability to climate scenarios

concepts.name: Climate Change–Migration–Security Nexus: Threat Multiplier Concept
key_dimensions: Pentagon/CNA Military Advisory Board reports framing climate as 'threat multiplier' for security
UNSC debates on climate-security: vetoed resolutions (Russia/China) on climate as security threat
Climate-induced resource scarcity → conflict → displacement pipeline: Sahel, Horn of Africa case studies
Securitization of climate migration vs. human rights-based approach — political tension

concepts.name: India's Vulnerability and Policy Position on Climate Refugees
key_dimensions: India not a signatory to 1951 Refugee Convention or 1967 Protocol — no domestic refugee law
India's own internal climate displacement: Sundarbans, coastal Odisha/Andhra, drought-prone regions
Cross-border dimension: Bangladesh climate migration to India — security vs. humanitarian framing
India's position in UNFCCC: equity, CBDR-RC, focus on adaptation finance over migration frameworks

concepts.name: Gender Dimensions of Climate Displacement: Women and Vulnerable Groups
key_dimensions: Women disproportionately affected by climate displacement: mobility restrictions, GBV in camps, livelihood loss
UNHCR-OHCHR joint framework: gender-responsive protection in climate displacement contexts
Child displacement: education disruption, trafficking risk, statelessness of children born to displaced parents
Intersection with SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities)

concepts.name: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) and Displacement Prevention
key_dimensions: Four priorities: understanding risk, governance, investment in DRR, preparedness — displacement prevention angle
Sendai Framework Monitor: tracks displacement as a DRR indicator
Relationship with Paris Agreement, SDGs, and Humanitarian Agenda — 'triple nexus' framework
Key distinction: Sendai focuses on disaster risk reduction (prevention), not on protecting already-displaced persons

concepts.name: Task Force on Displacement (TFD) under UNFCCC/Paris Agreement
key_dimensions: Established under Warsaw International Mechanism (WIM) for Loss and Damage — COP22 mandate
TFD recommendations (2018): integrate displacement into NDCs, NAPs, and humanitarian planning
WIM Executive Committee oversight — relationship between L&D mechanism and displacement
Gap: TFD recommendations are advisory; no binding obligations created under Paris Agreement for displaced persons
